type_hypothesis.against: Real evidence resists Type 3. (1) Moral vocabulary recurs across a decade, including private judgments of his own planned conduct: the 2017 diary rule that a reversed public commitment "was a lie" (C163) and "pretty morally bankrupt" about converting without Musk (C89, C206), "It just wasn't right" with anger denied (C35), the 2014 admission about treating "not the way I'd do it" as "bad" (C11), the charter learned "exactly right" (C20), and a fairness charge in the 2020 peer review (C32). (2) His self-descriptions stress environment and standards: 2014 (C182) and 2026 (C183). (3) Inside the 2019 essay itself he refused a face-saving excuse (C53), his frustrations were about correctness (C128, C158), and his stated reason to persist was understanding (C154), which fits One and Five. (4) His November 2023 verdict included a due-process complaint (C176, C180). (5) He hands off roles and does errands (C10, C70, C72, C73), and in 2026 described indecision and a weak sense of self (C39, C110), which fit Nine. (6) Much friction evidence is anonymous or rival-sourced (C30–C33, C92, C93) and his political reversal is explained by role incentives (C106, C189).
type_hypothesis.alternative_case: Type 1 is the strongest rival and the case is close. It explains the truthfulness rule and moral verdicts (C163, C89, C35), the judging habit (C11), the environment vision (C182, C183), the charter precision (C20), the refusal of an easy excuse and the correctness frustrations in the 2019 essay (C53, C128, C158), the due-process objection on November 17 (C176), the fairness charge in the 2020 review (C32), and nine years without a break as self-discipline (C111). Type 9 is a weaker third: his 2026 account of uncertainty and a weaker sense of self (C39, C110), accepting exclusion and offering to withdraw a review (C168, C170), and the jointly signed 2017 fear of harming the relationship (C25); it fails on the first-person record of setting a best-in-the-world bar, performing for evaluators and volunteering to run the founding (C04, C137, C14). Type 5 explains the 2019 study-before-acting and the understanding motive (C154, C156) but fails on a record full of performing, recruiting and public presentation (C159, C196). Type 6 can claim the fear language (C81, C155) and loyalty (C101) but shows little threat-scanning. Type 2 is undercut by his celebrating being unneeded and leaving Stripe (C70, C13, C71). Wing and subtype are omitted.
type_hypothesis.discriminator: How he keeps score on his own work. His moral vocabulary judges conduct, and that includes his own: in the private 2017 diary, a b-corp move he and his co-founders were weighing would be "a lie" or "morally bankrupt" (C163, C89, C206), and on November 17, 2023 he judged the board's action "wasn't right" (C35). That conduct-judging is conceded to the One reading (C207), with the limit that most people would condemn those acts, so it does not distinguish a One (C209). When he narrates his own work, without legal stakes, the measures are rank, notice and results: the "best in the world" bar he set for committing to any field, though impact decided which field (C04, C208, C64); reading and displaying what the audition evaluators wanted (C137, C138); "number 1 for a while" on his first Kaggle contest (C185); Goodfellow being impressed by his comments (C186); the recurring "validating" vocabulary (C16, C75, C76); "nothing to show for my efforts" and wanting to make "critical contributions" (C17, C151); and naming his obstacle as beginner status rather than error (C84, C86). The anonymous "ends-over-means" quote, the 2020 peer review, the trial mirror gloss and the PAC reversal are treated as non-discriminating or One-leaning (C105, C189). Limits: these are self-reports and self-presentation; a One can enjoy a ranking; the 2019 essay also contains One and Five evidence (C53, C158, C154); the Three lead holds for how he scores his work, not for how he judges conduct. The call would flip if new first-person evidence showed him scoring his own work mainly on rightness (C190).
type_hypothesis.unexplained: The moral vocabulary itself (C163, C89, C35), including the diary's private judgments of his own planned conduct (C206), and the environment self-descriptions (C182, C183) are conceded to the One reading rather than explained by the Three. The 2019 essay's refusal of an excuse and correctness frustrations (C53, C158) favor One. His emotion about loyalty (C36) and long record of errands (C72, C73) fit Two or Six as well. November 17, 2023 favors One or Six (C35, C176, C103). "So long as no one else is" (C22) mixes fairness and comparison. The 2024 loss of meaning after Sutskever left (C38, C194) fits Nine or Six as easily. The Sutskever memo (C34, C96) is unresolved; disputed rival-camp accounts not used in the article ("money and power," the 2017 idea of selling AGI to governments, which Brockman denies seriously entertaining) remain in the research record only, as does the ambiguously reported $100,000 donor admission.
